classes.name: National Assembly election (national ballot)
classes.locator: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996, s. 46 (350 to 400 members, proportional representation, national common voters roll) and s. 49 (five-year term)
classes.finest_note: Voting district for 1999 to 2024 (IEC Detailed Results and downloadable files); 1994 only as a PDF of provincial totals. Votes cast abroad are reported per mission.
classes.note: 400 members by closed-list proportional representation (Droop quota, largest remainders) over the whole country. From 1994 to 2019 one national ballot filled 200 seats from national lists and 200 from regional (provincial) lists; from 2024 (Electoral Amendment Act 1 of 2023) the national ballot fills the 200 compensatory seats so that the whole Assembly is proportional to it, and a separate regional ballot (class na_regional) fills the other 200. The 1994 election was held under the interim Constitution (Act 200 of 1993) over 26 to 29 April, with 27 April the main polling day.

cadence.locator: Constitution, s. 49(1) (five-year term) and (2) (election within 90 days of expiry or dissolution); Electoral Act 73 of 1998, s. 57 (result declared within seven days)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant seat is filled from the party's candidate list (Constitution, Schedule 6, and Electoral Act, Schedule 1A); there are no by-elections

classes.name: Election of the President by the National Assembly
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 86 (the National Assembly elects the President from among its members at its first sitting and to fill a vacancy) and Schedule 3, Part A (secret ballot presided over by a judge designated by the Chief Justice)
classes.note: A secret ballot of the 400 members with the Chief Justice or a designated judge presiding, held again in rounds if no candidate has a majority. Contested ballots so far: 2008 (Motlanthe), 2009, 2014, 2019, and 2024; Mandela (1994) and Mbeki (1999, 2004) and Ramaphosa (2018) were elected unopposed.

cadence.runoff_rule: Further rounds, the lowest candidate eliminated, until one has a majority of votes cast (Schedule 3, Part A)
cadence.locator: Constitution, s. 86 and Schedule 3, Part A
cadence.vacancy_rule: The National Assembly elects a new President within 30 days of a vacancy (s. 86(3))

classes.name: Election of the Premier by the provincial legislature
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 128 (the provincial legislature elects the Premier from among its members at its first sitting and to fill a vacancy) and Schedule 3
classes.note: Same procedure as the President's election, in each of the nine legislatures; the votes are announced at the sitting and recorded in the legislature's Hansard, not published by the IEC.

cadence.vacancy_rule: The legislature elects a new Premier within 30 days of a vacancy (s. 128(3))

dates.note: Nine elections after each general election (1994, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, 2024) and on vacancies; not yet counted from the legislatures' records.

classes.name: National Council of Provinces delegations
classes.locator: Constitution, ss. 60-61 and Schedule 3, Part B (ten delegates per province, six permanent and four special, allocated to parties in proportion to their seats in the legislature)
classes.disposition_reason: No vote is cast: each provincial legislature appoints its party-nominated delegates by the Schedule 3 formula from its own seat shares, and special delegates are designated from its members.

classes.name: Senate (interim Constitution)
classes.locator: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa Act 200 of 1993, ss. 48-49 (ten senators per province, nominated by the parties in each provincial legislature in proportion to their seats)
classes.disposition_reason: Senators were nominated by the parties in each provincial legislature in proportion to their seats; no ballot was cast. The Senate gave way to the National Council of Provinces in February 1997.

classes.name: Presiding officers of Parliament, the legislatures, and councils
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 52 (Speaker of the National Assembly), s. 64 (Chairperson of the NCOP), s. 111 (Speakers of the provincial legislatures), s. 160(1)(b) (municipal council chairpersons)
classes.disposition_reason: Internal votes of each house or council at its first sitting, recorded in its minutes or Hansard rather than run or published as elections.

classes.name: National and provincial referendums
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 84(2)(g) (the President calls a national referendum in terms of an Act of Parliament) and s. 127(2)(f) (the Premier calls a provincial referendum in accordance with national legislation)
classes.note: None has been held since 1994. Results would come from the Electoral Commission, which runs referendums (Electoral Commission Act 51 of 1996, s. 5).

cadence.locator: Electoral Commission Act 51 of 1996, s. 5(1)(a) (the Commission manages elections and referendums)

classes.name: Municipal council elections, proportional ballot
classes.locator: Local Government: Municipal Structures Act 117 of 1998, s. 22 and Schedule 1 (metropolitan and local councils with wards: half the councillors elected from party lists on a proportional ballot, compensating for ward seats); Constitution, s. 157
classes.finest_note: Voting district (IEC downloadable party results and Detailed Results).
classes.note: Each metropolitan (category A) and local (category B) council is half ward councillors and half list councillors; the PR ballot sets each party's total seats, less the wards it won.

cadence.locator: Constitution, s. 159 (term of no more than five years; election within 90 days of the term's expiry), as amended in 2003
cadence.vacancy_rule: A list seat is filled from the party's list; a dissolved council is re-elected in a by-election (Structures Act, s. 25)

cadence.locator: Constitution, s. 159; first elections of the new municipalities on 5 December 2000

classes.name: Municipal by-elections
classes.locator: Local Government: Municipal Structures Act 117 of 1998, s. 25 (by-elections within 90 days when a ward seat falls vacant, a council is dissolved, or an election is set aside)
classes.finest_note: Voting district (IEC by-election results by term, date, and type).
classes.note: Held most months, usually several wards on one day; a dissolved council is re-elected on both ballots.

cadence.vacancy_rule: By-election within 90 days of the vacancy

classes.name: Mayors, executive committees, and appointed district councillors
classes.locator: Municipal Structures Act 117 of 1998, ss. 23(1)(b) (district councillors appointed by local councils), 36 and 48 (council speakers), 43 and 55 (executive and executive mayors elected by the council)
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the councillors at council meetings (mayors, speakers, executive committees) or appointed by local councils to the district council; no public vote and no IEC result.

classes.name: Ward committees
classes.locator: Municipal Structures Act 117 of 1998, ss. 72-73 (ward committees of up to ten members chaired by the ward councillor, elected as the municipal council's rules provide)
classes.disposition_reason: Advisory bodies chosen at community meetings under each municipality's own rules; no state-run ballot and no published results.

classes.name: Traditional and Khoi-San councils (elected members)
classes.locator: Constitution, ss. 211-212 (recognition of traditional leadership and its role under national legislation); the Traditional and Khoi-San Leadership Act 3 of 2019 provides for a share of each council's members to be elected
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of the elected members are run by provincial departments of traditional affairs under provincial legislation; no official body publishes the results.

classes.name: National and provincial houses of traditional and Khoi-San leaders
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 212(2) (houses of traditional leaders established by national or provincial legislation)
classes.disposition_reason: Members are designated or elected by and from recognized traditional leaders, not by voters.

classes.name: School governing body elections
classes.locator: South African Schools Act 84 of 1996, ss. 23-31 (parents, educators, staff, and learners elect a governing body at each public school; three-year term)
classes.disposition_reason: Held at meetings of each school's parents and staff under provincial regulations; the electorates are not territorial and no results are published.

classes.name: Judges
classes.locator: Constitution, s. 174 (judges appointed by the President, on the advice of the Judicial Service Commission)

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.locator: Electoral Act 73 of 1998, ss. 27 and 31A-31B (parties submit candidate lists; independents qualify by signatures)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties compile their lists under their own constitutions; the state runs no primary and publishes no nominating vote.

classes.name: House of Assembly
classes.locator: South Africa Act 1909, ss. 32-34 and 40 (members elected in single-member electoral divisions); Republic of South Africa Constitution Act 110 of 1983, s. 41 (House of Assembly of the tricameral Parliament)
classes.note: First-past-the-post in single-member divisions; general elections in 1910, 1915, 1920, 1921, 1924, 1929, 1933, 1938, 1943, 1948, 1953, 1958, 1961, 1966, 1970, 1974, 1977, 1981, 1987, and 1989, with by-elections between. The franchise was white men (and qualified Cape and Natal voters of other races) in 1910, extended to white women in 1930; African voters in the Cape were moved to a separate roll in 1936 (three Native Representatives, 1937-1960) and Coloured voters in 1956 (four members, 1958-1970). From 1984 it was the white house of the tricameral Parliament.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the results digitally: the constituency returns appeared in the Government Gazette and official yearbooks, which no official host serves as data.

dates.note: Twenty general elections (15 September 1910 to 6 September 1989) and by-elections; not yet counted from an official record.

classes.name: House of Representatives and House of Delegates
classes.name_en: Tricameral Parliament: Coloured and Indian houses, 1984-1994
classes.locator: Republic of South Africa Constitution Act 110 of 1983, ss. 41-43 (House of Assembly, House of Representatives, and House of Delegates, each elected by its own voters' roll)
classes.note: Separate chambers elected by Coloured (House of Representatives, 80 elected members) and Indian (House of Delegates, 40 elected members) voters on separate rolls, by plurality in single-member divisions.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the constituency results; they appeared only in the Government Gazette.

dates.note: House of Representatives.
House of Delegates.
Both houses, with the House of Assembly.

classes.name: Senate
classes.locator: South Africa Act 1909, ss. 24-25 (eight senators per province elected by the members of the House of Assembly and the provincial council of each province, and eight nominated)
classes.disposition_reason: Senators were elected by electoral colleges of each province's members of the House of Assembly and provincial council, or nominated; no public vote. The Senate was abolished from 1 January 1981.

classes.name: Provincial councils
classes.locator: South Africa Act 1909, ss. 70-71 (a provincial council in each province elected by the parliamentary voters of the province)
classes.note: Elected from the same divisions and voters as the House of Assembly (the larger provinces used the parliamentary divisions), on their own three- to five-year cycle; abolished by the Provincial Government Act 69 of 1986.
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of the results; they appeared only in the provincial gazettes.

dates.note: Provincial council elections from 1910 to 1981; not yet counted from an official record.

classes.name: Referendums of white voters
classes.locator: Republic of South Africa Constitution Act 110 of 1983 (approved by the referendum of 2 November 1983)
classes.note: Three referendums of the white electorate: on becoming a republic (5 October 1960), on the 1983 constitution (2 November 1983), and on continuing negotiations (17 March 1992).
classes.disposition_reason: Results by voting region appeared in the Government Gazette; no official body publishes them as data.

classes.name: Separate representative councils
classes.name_en: Natives Representative Council, Coloured Persons Representative Council, South African Indian Council
classes.locator: Republic of South Africa Constitution Act 110 of 1983 (replaced the race-based councils with the House of Representatives and House of Delegates)
classes.note: Advisory councils elected on racial rolls: the Natives Representative Council (1937-1951, chosen by electoral colleges), the Coloured Persons Representative Council (elected 1969 and 1975, dissolved 1980), and the South African Indian Council (elected 1981).
classes.disposition_reason: No official digital publication of their results.

classes.name: Homeland legislative assemblies
classes.locator: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa Act 200 of 1993, s. 1(2) and Schedule 1 (the national territory includes the former Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Venda, and Ciskei, and the self-governing territories)
classes.note: Partly elected assemblies of the ten homelands, first Transkei (1963), and of the four (TBVC) declared independent by South African law; reincorporated on 27 April 1994.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were published, if at all, in the homeland governments' own gazettes, which no official host serves.

dates.note: Assembly elections in the ten homelands; not yet counted.

classes.name: Municipal, divisional, and black local authority elections before 1995
classes.locator: South Africa Act 1909, s. 85 (provincial councils legislate for municipal institutions and divisional councils)
classes.note: Councils elected under provincial ordinances on racially separate rolls, including black local authorities (1983 and 1988).
classes.disposition_reason: Run by each municipality or province; no official body publishes the results.

classes.name: Transitional local government elections
classes.locator: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa Act 200 of 1993, ss. 174-179 and 245 (local government elections under the Local Government Transition Act 209 of 1993)
classes.note: The first non-racial local elections, for transitional councils: 1 November 1995 in most of the country, 29 May 1996 in KwaZulu-Natal, and 26 June 1996 in the Cape metropolitan area and parts of the Western Cape. Run by provincial governments, not the IEC.
classes.disposition_reason: The IEC did not run these elections and its results site starts in 2000; no official body publishes the results.
